ideas.title: Certify continuation-aware tuple improvements
ideas.gap: Proxy scores lack a full-tree no-worsening guarantee.
ideas.hypothesis: Signed interval gates on old continuation moments yield unrestricted-tree improvement.

rationale.novelty: A specific derivative-coded full-tree safety/certification extension and explicit raw-flat threshold; ODE majorants and importance sampling are classical. Bounded primary-source comparison supports a scoped extension, not worldwide priority.
rationale.impact: The general support-safe policy-improvement framework addresses the recurring recursive-variance bottleneck; the exact explosion law is currently restricted to flat Allen-Cahn. Impact 10 describes that framework, not a claim of broad empirical transfer.
rationale.effect: Baseline: same raw flat Allen-Cahn estimator with uniform q. C8 and exact interval checks establish infinite variance at T=.5, lambda=.75 versus finite variance for supported p=.95; optimizing the rate separately gives an exact sqrt(1.9) horizon-threshold gain. This is a concrete capability change in a narrow benchmark, not a broad speedup.

feasibility.reason: The order comparison and exact binary control have a bounded proof/verification path.
feasibility.first_test: Attempt a counterexample to the gate; verify supported nonuniform flat controls.

ideas.baseline: Terminal proxy and raw uniform q
ideas.success_criterion: Replace heuristic acceptance with a useful sufficient variance-dominance certificate
